text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.69% today after rallying sharply over the past two days, pulling back from a near-term peak. The stock had climbed 5.4% in just two days (October 14–15) as crude oil prices surged on Middle East tensions and supply concerns, but today's decline reflects profit-taking and some cooling in oil prices — U.S. crude dropped to near $98 a barrel as traders reassessed the geopolitical risk after Iran's initial attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The underlying refining environment remains supportive despite today's pullback. U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain tight (especially diesel, which hit record high prices in September), and the IEA announcement to release strategic diesel reserves suggests persistent tightness in the market — all of which typically benefit a major refiner's margins when they can convert crude into products that command premium prices.
